text:
sara-support: Customer on Cloudflare Workers reporting SSE stream from our /v1/streams endpoint is arriving with a truncated final JSON chunk when Cloudflare applies gzip. They then reconnect and see the missing tail as a duplicate chunk; billing shows tokens for both. Need quick repro + triage.

 dmitri: Can you paste a minimal repro and any request IDs/trace ids?

 sara-support: Repro steps from customer (short):
 1) Simple CF Worker that fetches our stream and pipes response to client.
 2) Worker does not set Accept-Encoding, CF edge adds gzip.
 3) Client (EventSource) sometimes gets an incomplete last "data:" line (missing trailing chars / closing brace).
 4) If client reconnects immediately, it sees the missing tail as an additional "data" event and billing shows both chunks.

 CF Worker snippet they provided:
 ```js
 addEventListener('fetch', event => event.respondWith(handle(event.request)))
 async function handle(req) {
   const r = await fetch('https://api.redwood.com/v1/streams?model=gpt-test', {
     headers: { 'Accept': 'text/event-stream' }
   })
   return r
 }
 ```

 Observed payload (client-side):
 data: {"id":"c1","delta":"Hello, worl

 // connection closes unexpectedly here 

 On reconnect: 
 data: {"id":"c1","delta":"d"}
 data: [DONE]

 So final JSON gets split/duplicated across reconnects and occasionally arrives truncated.

 anya: Do we emit Content-Encoding: gzip from our side? We shouldn't be compressing chunked SSE. Need to check proxy/edge behavior + Transfer-Encoding: chunked. Also please attach the trace ids.

 sara-support: Two trace ids from the customer: trace=abc123:2026 and trace=def456:2026. They also ran curl --no-compress which fixed it on their side (no truncation).

 eng-ryan: Interesting — this sounds like Cloudflare is re-chunking/compressing the stream and closing in the middle of a compression block, so the EventSource on client sees an incomplete decompression result. Workaround: set Accept-Encoding: identity or Cache-Control: no-transform to prevent edge compression. Can you confirm if the customer tried Accept-Encoding: identity?

 sara-support: Yes — customer tried adding `Accept-Encoding: identity` in the Worker fetch and the stream came through intact, no truncated final chunk and no duplicate on reconnect.

 dmitri: Ok that's a good mitigant. Next steps for us: reproduce on a staging CF Worker + our staging v1/streams with gzip enabled, capture raw TCP/bytes to confirm a compression block cut. If confirmed, escalate to eng-runtime/edge infra for a fix or guidance for docs. I'll take this and tag eng-runtime.

 infra-bot: Created INC-2026: "Edge compression + SSE: CF Worker gzip re-chunking leads to truncated final frame and duplicate tokens on reconnect" (priority P2).

 eng-ryan: For immediate customer help we should document the Accept-Encoding: identity workaround and add a short note in streaming docs (warning about intermediary compression). Also check if our CDN/proxy has any config that could cause compression on SSE responses.

 dmitri: I'll try to reproduce today. If I can repro, I'll include a pcap and raw decompressed bytes for runtime. ETA 24h.

 sara-support: Thanks team — shared workaround with customer and asked them to switch to identity until we have a definitive fix.

 anya: Also adding a quick unit in the troubleshooting page: "If you see truncated SSE frames on Cloudflare or similar proxies, try Accept-Encoding: identity or no-transform."

 dmitri: Assigning to @eng-ryan and eng-runtime if repro confirmed.

 eng-ryan: Acknowledged.

 sara-support: Closing the loop with customer; will update INC-2026 with customer repro files when they upload. :thumbsup:
